true_positives.golden_comment: The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Redefining self.downsize overrides the existing four-argument method

Ruby does not support overloading, so the new def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={}) replaces the previous def self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={}). Any caller using OptimizedImage.downsize(path, out, width, height) now binds width as dimensions and height as opts. The next downsize call may then evaluate opts[:allow_animation] on an Integer and raise TypeError, or silently ignore the height. Remove one of the duplicate methods and provide a single supported signature.

true_positives.golden_comment: Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Client upload validation hardcodes 10 MB instead of per-type site settings

validateUploadedFile no longer reads Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so both image and attachment client-side checks now use 10 MB. The 413 handler at line 246 does the same instead of using max_image_size_kb. Sites with a smaller configured limit still allow the browser to submit oversized files, while sites with a larger configured limit have valid uploads blocked by the client. The alert text can also report the wrong maximum size. Keep using the site settings or add a separate consistent cap.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.
The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.

false_positives.candidate:
Animated GIFs are flattened because downsize sees the tempfile path, not the original filename

OptimizedImage.downsize decides whether to use the animated downsize path by testing the source path for a .GIF extension in OptimizedImage.optimize. Here the source path is tempfile.path, which for Rack uploads is typically a generated /tmp/RackMultipart... path without the original .gif extension, while the original filename is available separately. As a result, oversized animated GIF uploads are processed by the normal ImageMagick instructions with from[0], which reads only the first frame and throws away the animation. The original filename/extension must be preserved on the tempfile or passed into the downsize call so the animated branch can be selected.

Automatic downsize ignores conversion failure and final size

The loop calls OptimizedImage.downsize and decrements attempt, but ignores the boolean returned by downsize and never checks after the loop whether tempfile.size is still greater than SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes. If ImageMagick/gifsicle fails (corrupt image, mislabeled non-image, unsupported format) or five 80% reductions are insufficient, create_upload proceeds with the same tempfile. This can reject the upload only later with a generic error, or store an oversized/corrupt image depending on the rest of the model validation. The code should break on successful downsize and return an explicit error if the final file is still over the limit.

No tests added for auto-downsize behavior

The PR adds server-side downsize-on-upload, changes OptimizedImage method signatures, and changes client validation, but no specs are included. Boundaries around max_image_size_kb, downsize failure, insufficient reduction, animated GIFs, and non-image uploads are untested. A test for the previous OptimizedImage.downsize call style would also have caught the duplicate method issue.

OptimizedImage.optimize signature change breaks positional width/height callers

optimize changed from optimize(operation, from, to, width, height, opts={}) to optimize(operation, from, to, dimensions, opts={}). Direct callers that still pass width and height as two arguments will now have height treated as opts, causing TypeError when opts[:allow_animation] is evaluated or otherwise incorrect behavior. If this is meant as an internal API, make that explicit and update all consumers; otherwise keep a backwards-compatible shim.

URL download limit is hardcoded to 10 MB and ignores site settings

FileHelper.download now uses 10.megabytes instead of SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes. Non-image URL uploads do not go through the later image downsize loop, so this action can fetch up to 10 MB even if the configured max_image_size_kb is much lower. Conversely, sites with max_image_size_kb above 10 MB can no longer fetch such files via URL. Use the configured limit for non-image uploads or enforce it explicitly after download.

true_positives.golden_comment: The EmbeddableHost model's before_validation callback calls self.host.sub! to strip http://, https://, and path segments, but if self.host is nil, this raises NoMethodError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
before_validation crashes when host is nil

`before_validation` calls `self.host.sub!` before any presence or format validations run. If a request creates or updates an `EmbeddableHost` with a missing/null `host`, this raises `NoMethodError` on nil and returns a 500 instead of a normal validation error. The callback should guard with `self.host.to_s` or a presence validation should be added before mutation.

true_positives.golden_comment: The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Missing records and malformed params cause 500 errors

`update` and `destroy` use `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first`, which can be nil for an unknown ID. `update` then passes nil to `save_host` and calls `host.host=`, while `destroy` calls `host.destroy`, both raising `NoMethodError`. Additionally, `save_host` unconditionally dereferences `params[:embeddable_host]`, so malformed input without that root key also raises. These should return 404/JSON errors instead of 500s.

true_positives.golden_comment: Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Legacy embeddable hosts are inserted without normalization and will not match the new host check

The old `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts` values could include full URLs and paths, as shown by the removed specs using `http://discourse.org` and `https://example.com/1234`. This migration inserts each `h` verbatim into `embeddable_hosts.host`, but `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?`/`record_for_host` parses the incoming referer and compares only `uri.host` to the stored `lower(host)`. A migrated value like `http://example.com` will never match `example.com`, so existing full-URL host configurations silently stop allowing embeds after upgrade.

true_positives.golden_comment: The contents of `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` have been swapped, resulting in the loss of original category fabricators and potentially causing errors in fabricator usage.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Category and embeddable host fabricator contents were swapped

`spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` now defines `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)`, while `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` contains the `:category`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category`, and `:private_category` definitions. This looks like an accidental file-swap. It may work in the full suite if all fabricator files are loaded, but the file named `category_fabricator` no longer defines `:category` and direct requires or future maintenance will be broken. The contents should be moved back.

false_negatives.golden_comment: record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

The SQL query in the `app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb` file uses string interpolation (`'#{h}'`) to insert values, which is vulnerable to SQL injection. It should use parameter binding or proper quoting to prevent this security vulnerability.

The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.

false_positives.candidate:
GET /fruits/:id always returns the first fruit, so the id-2 test exercises the wrong record

The test changed to `store.find('fruit', 2)` and asserts `fruitCols.length` is 2 with color ids 1 and 2, but this pretender route always sets `const fruit = fruits[0]` regardless of the requested id. The assertion therefore still validates fruit id 1, not fruit id 2's actual single-color array, and would not catch errors in the plural `_ids` hydration for a single element.

Hosts saved with a port can never match

The host format validation allows an optional `:port` (line 2), and `before_validation` does not strip it. However `record_for_host` compares only `uri.host` to the stored `lower(host)`, ignoring `uri.port`. A host entered as `example.com:8080` will therefore never match `http://example.com:8080`. Either reject ports in the validation or include the port in the lookup comparison.

No action-level tests for embeddable host admin CRUD

The new admin controller specs only assert that the controllers inherit from `Admin::AdminController`. They do not exercise `create`, `update`, or `destroy`, staff authorization, invalid host input, missing categories, or missing-record behavior. Since this PR introduces a new admin CRUD API and changes embedding access control, these cases should be covered.

true_positives.golden_comment: logic: Potential nil pointer exception - if no TopicUser record exists, tu will be nil and calling methods on it will crash
true_positives.matched_candidate:
unsubscribe crashes when the current user has no TopicUser record

`TopicUser.find_by` returns nil if the current user has never interacted with this topic, which is possible when the URL is visited directly or from a stale email. The next line calls `tu.notification_level`, raising `NoMethodError` and returning a 500 before any notification level is changed. Use `TopicUser.find_or_initialize_by(...)` or `TopicUser.change` so a missing record is created instead of crashing.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Typo in property name: 'stopNotificiationsText' should be 'stopNotificationsText' (missing 'n' in 'Notifications')

false_positives.candidate:
No tests for new unsubscribe action, route, or per-topic email link

The only test change supplies `unsubscribe_url` to an existing builder example but does not assert that the per-topic unsubscribe link appears in the body. There are no controller/request specs for `TopicsController#unsubscribe` (authentication, slug redirects, missing TopicUser, notification-level transitions) or for the Ember route/template. The new behavior can break without detection.

Per-topic unsubscribe changes state via GET without CSRF or token

The new `unsubscribe` action is a GET route that modifies `TopicUser.notification_level`. A logged-in user's browser can be made to request `/t/<slug>/<id>/unsubscribe` from a third-party page, and because the action is not protected by CSRF or a token, the change will be applied. An attacker can mute or downgrade notification settings for arbitrary topics for a victim. Use a signed/one-time token in the email link or require a CSRF-protected POST.

Top-level topicUnsubscribe route will not resolve the nested unsubscribe template

The route is declared as a top-level route named `topicUnsubscribe`, so Ember's default template name is `topic-unsubscribe` (or `topicUnsubscribe`), not `topic/unsubscribe`. The added template is at `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs`, which would match a nested `topic.unsubscribe` route. Since the route does not override `renderTemplate`, the unsubscribe page will not render its client-side content. Move the template to `templates/topic-unsubscribe.hbs` or declare `unsubscribe` as a nested route under `topic`.

Unsubscribe copy promises full stop but controller only lowers to regular The string says "You will stop receiving notifications for {{title}}." However the controller sets a watching/tracking user to `regular` on the first click, and `regular` still permits notifications such as replies and mentions. Users may believe they are fully unsubscribed while still receiving some notifications. Either set `muted` for a true unsubscribe or change the copy to describe changing notification state.

unsubscribe_link interpolation now requires unsubscribe_url but MessageBuilder has no fallback

`server.en.yml` changed `unsubscribe_link` to interpolate `%{unsubscribe_url}`. `MessageBuilder` only populates that key if the caller passed `unsubscribe_url` in opts. Any existing `Email::MessageBuilder` use with `add_unsubscribe_link: true` but no `unsubscribe_url` will now get an I18n missing interpolation error in both `html_part` (line 67) and `body` (line 90). Since this is a shared builder, provide a safe default/guard or update all callers and fail explicitly before building the mail.

true_positives.golden_comment: BlockedEmail.should_block_email? method has side effects during a read operation - it updates statistics even when just checking if an email should be blocked. This could cause race conditions in concurrent environments and makes the method name misleading.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
should_block? has DB write side effects and double counts per attempt

BlockedEmail.should_block? increments match_count and calls record.save whenever a matching record is found. EmailValidator calls it during User validation; UsersController#create calls user.valid? before user.save, and save runs validations again, so one blocked signup attempt increments and saves the BlockedEmail row twice. The read-modify-write is also not atomic, so concurrent attempts can lose increments. Track match statistics after a real signup attempt (or use an atomic update) and avoid writing in a validation predicate.

true_positives.golden_comment: The case-sensitive email lookup in `BlockedEmail.should_block?` creates a bypass risk, allowing 'User@Example.com' to bypass a block on 'user@example.com'. This can lead to unauthorized access to blocked users.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Blocked email lookup is case-sensitive and unnormalized

BlockedEmail.should_block? uses BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first with the raw submitted value. Elsewhere the app normalizes email addresses via Email.downcase (and change_email also strips), but this check does not. On PostgreSQL the unique index is case-sensitive, so a block stored as foo@example.com can be bypassed by submitting Foo@example.com, and duplicate case-variant block records can be created. Normalize the address before lookup and before persistence.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The regex pattern @(#{domains}) in email_in_restriction_setting? method only matches domain suffixes, not full domains with proper boundary anchoring. An attacker can register evil.example.com to bypass a whitelist entry for example.com.

false_positives.candidate:
Any server email error is cached as rejected, not just block-list failures

On a failed create, any presence of result.errors.email causes result.values.email to be pushed into rejectedEmails. Server errors can include uniqueness (already has been taken), domain whitelist/blacklist, blocked-list, or other failures, but the client will later show every such address as user.email.invalid. It also never removes entries. Cache only a machine-readable blocked-email rejection or clear rejectedEmails after the specific issue is resolved.

change_email sends confirmation for blocked email before validation

change_email creates an EmailToken for lower_email and enqueues the authorize_email job without checking BlockedEmail.should_block? or otherwise running email validation. Because the new block validator only runs when a User record's email is changed and saved, a blocked email can receive a confirmation/authorization email before any model validation occurs. Add an explicit BlockedEmail check in change_email and reject the request before creating the token or enqueuing mail.

rejectedEmails is shared mutable state and never reset

Defining rejectedEmails: Em.A([]) on the controller class creates one shared Ember array rather than a per-instance array. Because createAccount only pushes into it and there is no clearing on successful account creation or modal close, an email rejected during one attempt remains rejected for later attempts in the same long-lived controller instance. Define the array in init or clear it when the signup form is reset.

true_positives.golden_comment: The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
true_positives.matched_candidate: URL is interpolated into HTML without escaping The imported-from footer builds `#{url}` with the raw URL. A URL such as `http://example.com/'>` passes the `https?://` regex and breaks out of the attribute before being stored as raw HTML. This is an independent HTML/script injection vector and should be HTML-escaped or constructed with a safe helper.

true_positives.golden_comment: The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Invalid ERB syntax `<%- end if %>` will break rendering

The `if` block is closed as `end if` with no condition, which is not valid ERB/Ruby and will fail the embed page. This template is the success path for `/embed/best`; requests for an existing topic will error instead of rendering comments.

true_positives.golden_comment: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
PollFeed assumes every feed item has `content`

`i.content.scrub` raises `NoMethodError` when an RSS item uses the common `<description>` element or has no content instead of `content:encoded`. The importer should fall back to `i.content || i.description` and skip entries where both are blank.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

false_positives.candidate:
Disqus import loses original thread creation time

The previous importer passed `created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at])` when creating the initial topic. The new `TopicEmbed.import_remote` path does not accept or set `created_at`, so imported topics are stamped with the current time while replies still use their original timestamps, breaking chronological ordering.

Imported raw HTML is rendered unescaped

`post.cooked` is emitted with `raw`. Imported posts are created with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, and `Post#cook` now returns `raw` directly for that method, bypassing Discourse's normal cooking/sanitization. RSS or readability content can therefore contain executable `<script>`/event-handler markup that runs in the Discourse origin for every visitor of the embedded comments.

Remote reads have no timeout

`open(url).read` uses default open/read timeouts, so a slow or stalled source can block a Sidekiq worker indefinitely. PollFeed has the same issue at `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:29`. Use explicit `open_timeout` and `read_timeout` values or another HTTP client with timeout support.

Throttle key expiry is not atomic with creation

`setnx` followed by `expire` has a crash window between the two calls that can leave the `retrieved:<url>` key with no TTL. That URL would then be throttled forever. Use an atomic NX+EX set (or a Lua script/MULTI) so the key is always created with an expiry.

fetch_http calls `.downcase` without checking `embed_by_username`

`SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase` can fail with `NoMethodError` when the setting is nil/unset, which the controller and RetrieveTopic do not prevent. PollFeed guards this setting with `present?` before polling, but `TopicRetriever#fetch_http` does not. Add a blank check and return early before querying.

true_positives.golden_comment: -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
order mixin maps modern order values directly to 2009 box-ordinal-group

The 2009 `-webkit-box-ordinal-group` / `-moz-box-ordinal-group` properties start at 1, while modern `order` starts at 0. Passing the modern value unchanged means `order(1)` would map to ordinal group 1, the same as default siblings, and `order(0)` would be invalid in the old model. The old fallback should add 1 to the value. The current calls use 2 and 3 and happen to work, but the generic mixin is incorrect and will break when reused with 0 or 1.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.
-ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.

false_positives.candidate:
Header panel right alignment depends on modern flexbox auto margins

`.panel` is no longer floated and is right-aligned only via `margin-left: auto` inside `.contents`, which the new `flexbox()` mixin turns into a flex container. That mixin also emits legacy `display: -webkit-box` / `-moz-box` fallbacks, but 2009 flexbox does not use auto margins for main-axis packing. Since no `box-pack: end` or equivalent fallback is provided, browsers that use those legacy declarations will not keep the panel right-aligned. If the fallbacks are meant to be supported, the header controls will be misplaced there.

align-items mixin omits Mozilla 2009 flexbox alignment fallback

`flexbox()` and `inline-flex()` emit `display: -moz-box` / `-moz-inline-box` fallbacks, but this `align-items` mixin emits `-webkit-box-align` for the 2009 box model without emitting `-moz-box-align`. As a result, Firefox versions using the `-moz-box` fallback will not get the intended `center` alignment for header `.contents` or `.small-action`, nor the `baseline` alignment for `.badge-wrapper.bullet`.

small-action button no longer right-aligned

`.small-action` is now a flex container, so its children, including this `button`, are flex items. Floats do not apply to flex items, so `float: right` is ignored. There is also no `margin-left: auto`, `flex-grow`, or `order` on the preceding `.small-action-desc` or the button to push it to the right edge, so the button will sit immediately after the description content instead of being right-aligned. This regresses the existing small-action post layout.

true_positives.golden_comment: The include_website_name method is missing the required ? suffix. Rails serializers expect include_ methods to end with ? for conditional attribute inclusion, a convention followed by other methods in this serializer. Without it, the website_name attribute may not be conditionally included as intended. Additionally, the '.' << website_host string concatenation should be replaced with '.' + website_host or '.#{website_host}' to avoid mutating string literals, which can lead to issues.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
include_website_name is missing `?` and has no effect

ActiveModel Serializer conditional inclusion methods are named `include_<attribute>?` (see `include_email?` and `include_stats?` in this same file). The new method is `def include_website_name` without the trailing question mark, so it is never consulted during serialization. As a result, `website_name` is always included, producing `website_name: null` for users with no website or an unparsable website value instead of omitting the key. Rename it to `include_website_name?` or remove it in favor of the generated untrusted-attributes include method.

false_positives.candidate:
website_name leaks hidden website info for anonymous TL0 users

`website_name` was added to the serialized attributes but was not added to `untrusted_attributes` (lines 105-111). `website_name` is derived from `website`, so even when the existing untrusted-attribute restriction suppresses the `website` key for anonymous visitors viewing a TL0 profile, the serializer still computes and emits `website_name`. This reveals the host and path of a website that is supposed to be hidden. Add `:website_name` to `untrusted_attributes` and make sure any manual `include_website_name?` does not override the generated restriction; the spec's untrusted attributes list should also be updated.

true_positives.golden_comment: In .topic-meta-data h5 a, the original code had color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) but was changed to dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)). true_positives.golden_comment: In the next action, capping the next offset at user_count can produce an empty page (e.g., total equal to limit results in offset == total, showing 2/2 with no members). This can cause confusing UX on the last page.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Pagination computes an extra page for exact multiples

totalPages uses Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1. When user_count is a positive multiple of limit (for example 50 users with limit 50), this returns 2 instead of 1. As a result the first page is not treated as the last page, Next sets offset to user_count, and the UI shows an empty second page. Use Math.ceil(user_count / limit).

false_negatives.golden_comment: The findMembers() call is now asynchronous and unhandled. The controller may not have member data immediately available, creating a race condition.

false_positives.candidate:
Group create ignores alias_level from the client

The client Group#asJSON sends alias_level and the admin form always displays the alias level combo for new groups, but create only sets name and visible. A new group saved with a non-default alias level is persisted with the default alias_level 0; the client model is only updated with the id from the response, so the UI continues showing the unsaved selection. Assign group.alias_level from params if present.

Member list iterates controller property `members` instead of the group's members

The group-members route now sets the controller model to the Group object and calls model.findMembers(), which populates model.members. This template iterates `members` directly. The route does not set a controller property named `members`, so with the generated route controller the list will be empty. Iterate `model.members` or expose `members` on the controller.

No spec for the paginated public members JSON contract

GroupsController#members changed from rendering a serialized member array to returning a custom {members, meta} object with limit, offset, and meta.total for all groups. This is a public API contract change, but no controller spec in the PR covers the JSON shape, default limit, offset, total, or authorization/visibility behavior.

Usernames are split on comma but not stripped

The client sends a comma-separated string. If it contains spaces, e.g. 'alice, bob', split(',') yields ' bob' and User.find_by_username(' bob') returns nil. The request then succeeds but silently skips valid users. Strip each username after splitting before lookup.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The @loaded_locales instance variable in translate_accelerator.rb is lazily initialized and accessed by multiple concurrent threads without synchronization.

Consider normalizing the input locale (e.g., to a symbol) when checking/loading here to avoid double-loading if the same locale is passed as a String vs Symbol (also applies to other locations in the PR).

false_positives.candidate:
Fallback locales are loaded only for controller requests

`I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!` is only called from `ApplicationController#set_locale`. `I18n.translate` in `lib/freedom_patches/translate_accelerator.rb` lazy-loads only the current locale via `load_locale(config.locale)`, so translations performed outside controller actions (for example mailers, background jobs, or rake tasks) with a non-default locale will not have the site-default or `:en` YAML loaded before fallback lookup runs. A missing key in the current locale can then fail or produce an I18n missing-translation error instead of falling back. The fallback preloading must happen wherever `I18n.locale` is set, or `translate` should load the fallback chain itself.

No tests cover the new fallback behavior

This PR introduces a custom fallback order, loads fallbacks and pluralization in a new initializer, removes environment-specific fallback flags, and adds `ensure_loaded!` wiring, but no specs are added. The behavior should be tested: anonymous users use the site default, logged-in users fall back in the expected order, fallback locale YAMLs are actually loaded, and non-controller translation paths do not regress. Without tests, this lazy-loading/fallback interaction is easy to break.

Translation cache key ignores the fallback chain

The cached translation key is `"#{key}#{config.locale}#{config.backend.object_id}"`. With the new fallback chain `[locale, SiteSetting.default_locale.to_sym, :en]`, a translation that is missing in the requested locale can be resolved from a fallback locale and then cached under the requested locale. If `SiteSetting.default_locale` changes at runtime, the same key and locale would need a different fallback resolution, but the old cached value is still returned until `I18n.reload!` clears the cache. This can serve stale translations after an admin changes the default locale. Include the fallback chain in the cache key or invalidate the translation cache when the default locale changes.

true_positives.golden_comment: The OptimizedCursorPaginator in organization_auditlogs.py attempts to use negative slice offsets on Django querysets, but Django querysets do not support negative slicing and will raise an AssertionError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Negative offset pagination slices a Django QuerySet with a negative start

When enable_advanced_features is true and cursor.offset < 0, start_offset is set to the negative cursor offset and the code executes queryset[start_offset:stop]. Django QuerySet slicing does not support negative indexes and raises ValueError ("Negative indexing is not supported."), so the advertised negative-offset reverse pagination cannot work. A request such as cursor=0:-1:0&optimized_pagination=true from an authorized user will produce a server error instead of a page or a clean 400.

true_positives.golden_comment: get_item_key assumes a numeric key, but the paginator is used with order_by=-datetime in the audit logs endpoint; calling math.floor/ceil on a datetime will raise a TypeError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
OptimizedCursorPaginator cannot handle datetime ordering used by audit logs

get_item_key() calls math.floor() or math.ceil() on the value of self.key. When OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint uses OptimizedCursorPaginator with order_by="-datetime", this value is a datetime, so math.floor(datetime) raises TypeError: must be real number, not datetime. Any non-empty audit-log page requested with optimized_pagination=true by an allowed user will return a 500 instead of results. Additionally, value_from_cursor() returns cursor.value directly rather than converting it to a datetime like DateTimePaginator does, so cursor comparisons are not correct for datetime keys.

false_negatives.golden_comment: When requests are authenticated with API keys or org auth tokens (which have user_id=None), organization_context.member is None. Line 71 attempts to access organization_context.member.has_global_access without checking if member is None, causing an AttributeError crash when optimized_pagination=true is used, even though the request passed all permission checks with valid org:write scope.
Importing non-existent OptimizedCursorPaginator

No tests cover the new OptimizedCursorPaginator or the endpoint opt-in path

The PR adds a new paginator with custom slicing and offset behavior and a new endpoint feature flag but does not change any tests. This leaves both the datetime ordering failure and the negative slice failure uncovered, so CI would not catch a broken optimized-pagination flow.

true_positives.golden_comment: OptimizedCursorPaginator's negative-offset branch in get_result() passes cursor.offset directly as start_offset to queryset slicing when enable_advanced_features is True and cursor.offset < 0.
true_positives.matched_candidate:

Django QuerySets do not support negative slicing; this raises ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported. The audit log endpoint enables this flag, and cursor offsets are user-controlled strings parsed by Cursor.from_string, so a request with a negative cursor offset will produce a 500 instead of paginating.

true_positives.golden_comment: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key uses floor/ceil on a datetime key (order_by='-datetime'), causing TypeError.
true_positives.matched_candidate:

OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint now allows OptimizedCursorPaginator with order_by="-datetime". That paginator is a copy of the numeric Paginator: get_item_key does math.floor/math.ceil on the attribute, and value_from_cursor returns the raw cursor number. AuditLogEntry.datetime is a datetime, so after fetching rows build_cursor calls math.floor(datetime) and raises TypeError; if a numeric cursor value is provided, build_queryset also compares a timestamp column to a number, causing a SQL operator error. false_positives.candidate:
Buffer storage changes from Redis set to sorted set without migration

process_spans now executes ZADD against span-buf:s:*, and _load_segment_data/add-buffer.lua now use ZSCAN/ZCARD/ZUNIONSTORE. The previous version stored these keys as Redis sets with SADD/SUNIONSTORE. During a rolling deploy, keys written by the old code before the deploy still have type set; the first ZADD or ZCARD on those keys returns WRONGTYPE, failing span processing and causing retries until the old keys expire. There is no migration, key-format versioning, or cleanup for existing set-typed keys.

Eviction can remove the segment root span producing invalid segments

After merging, the script does zpopmin(set_key, span_count - 1000) to keep only 1000 spans. The lowest score is the oldest end_timestamp_precise, and the segment/root span is frequently the oldest member. If the root span is popped, the remaining set can contain child spans whose parent_span_id/segment_id refers to the removed root, but no span with span_id == segment_key; the flush path then emits a segment with segment_id set and no is_segment=True span. This silently corrupts/incompletes the segment. The cap is also hardcoded to 1000 while SpansBuffer.max_segment_spans defaults to 1001 and is now unused, so configuration cannot control this behavior.

No tests cover insertion-time eviction or sorted-set migration

The tests were updated to pass end_timestamp_precise, but no test exercises the new sorted-set eviction path: inserting >1000 spans, verifying the cap is applied, checking that the root span is not evicted, or verifying that old set-typed keys are migrated/handled. Given the data-integrity risks in this change, this behavior should be covered.

false_negatives.golden_comment: In _set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling(), the check `if client_sample_rate:` treats 0.0 as falsy, so a sample_rate of 0.0 is silently skipped and never set on normalized_data.

Using Python’s built-in hash() to build cache keys is non-deterministic across processes (hash randomization), so keys won’t match across workers and invalidate_upsampling_cache may fail to delete them. Use a deterministic serialization of project_ids for the cache key.

The upsampling eligibility check passes the outer dataset instead of the actual dataset used by scoped_dataset. In paths where the query ultimately runs against discover (e.g., dashboard split) while the original dataset is metrics, upsampling may be skipped even when all projects are allowlisted.

false_positives.candidate:
Accidental submodule/gitlink committed

The PR adds a `sentry-repo` gitlink/submodule entry pointing at commit `a5d290951def84afdcc4c88d2f1f20023fc36e2a`. There is no related `.gitmodules` change and no code uses it; this looks accidental. Committing a submodule tracking the base commit can make clones fail or leave the working tree dirty and should be removed before merge.

Error-focused query check uses naive substring matching

`_is_error_focused_query` returns True whenever the lowercased query string contains `event.type:error`. A negated query (`!event.type:error`), a mixed query (`event.type:error OR event.type:transaction`), or a quoted literal (`message:"event.type:error"`) all satisfy this check. For Discover, that makes `count()` get rewritten to `upsampled_count()`/`sum(sample_weight)` for rows that are not error events; transaction rows may not have meaningful sample_weight, leading to incorrect counts or Snuba errors. Parse the actual query terms (and handle negation/quotes) instead of substring matching.

Transaction event not flushed before Snuba query

In `test_error_upsampling_with_transaction_events`, a transaction is stored via `self.store_event(...)` after the setUp wait calls, but no `wait_for_event_count` is issued for it before the API request. Snuba indexing is asynchronous, so `data[0][1][0]["count"] == 1` can race and fail. Wait for the transaction to be indexed (for example `self.wait_for_event_count(self.project.id, 2)`) before querying.

Upsampling eligibility uses request query rather than executed query

`_get_event_stats` receives the actual `query` being executed, but `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` only inspects `request.GET["query"]` inside `_is_error_focused_query` for the Discover dataset. In `get_event_stats_factory`, dashboard widget discover-split paths call `_get_event_stats` with rewritten queries such as `errors_only_query` (`... AND !event.type:transaction`) or `transactions_only_query` (`... AND event.type:transaction`). The helper can therefore decide an error-only split is not error-focused (undercounting) or decide a transaction-only split is error-focused (applying sample_weight to transactions). Pass the actual `query` string to the eligibility helper or derive the dataset/event type from the query being executed.

Similarly, timestamp=0 with age is not rejected. Presence should be checked with `in self.initial_data` or `is not None`. Also both age and timestamp are currently optional, so reports with neither are accepted; if exactly one is required by the Reporting API specs this endpoint claims to support, add that validation.

true_positives.golden_comment: Because backupCodes are decrypted and mutated in memory before being written back, two concurrent login requests using the same backupCode could both pass this check and update, so a single backup code may effectively be accepted more than once if used concurrently, weakening the intended one-time-use semantics.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Backup code single-use consumption is not atomic

The code reads `user.backupCodes`, validates the submitted code with `indexOf`, and then later writes the whole array back with the matched index set to `null`. There is no transaction or conditional update. Two concurrent requests using the same backup code can both pass validation before either write happens, so both sessions are authorized. Requests using different backup codes can also lose updates because each writes a stale array, leaving an already-used code active. The one-time-code guarantee should be enforced with an atomic/conditional update.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The exported function TwoFactor handles backup codes and is in BackupCode.tsx. Inconsistent naming.
Error message mentions 'backup code login' but this is a disable endpoint, not login

Object URL for backup codes is not revoked on component unmount, leading to a potential memory leak. This can cause increased memory usage over time, especially if the component is mounted and unmounted frequently.

false_positives.candidate:
Backup code login bypasses password when a totpCode is also supplied

The password verification block at line 121 only runs when `credentials.totpCode` is falsy. The new backup-code branch at line 131 is chosen whenever `credentials.backupCode` is present, and it never verifies the password itself. A caller can therefore authenticate with `email`, a valid `backupCode`, and any non-empty `totpCode` (for example `000000`): the truthy `totpCode` skips password verification, then the backup code is validated and authorize returns the user. A stolen/leaked backup code alone becomes sufficient to sign in, defeating two-factor protection.

First 2FA enable test does not close the new backup-code screen before asserting state

`handleEnable` now leaves the modal on the new `DisplayBackupCodes` screen and does not call `onEnable` until the `backup-codes-close` button is clicked. This test enters the OTP and immediately asserts the two-factor switch is checked, so it checks state before the parent is notified/refetched. The second test was updated to click `backup-codes-close` and assert `data-state="checked"`; this test should do the same. true_positives.golden_comment: A null reference occurs in GoogleCalendarService.createEvent() and updateEvent() when mainHostDestinationCalendar is destructured from evt.destinationCalendar but evt.destinationCalendar is null or an empty array, causing mainHostDestinationCalendar to be undefined.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Google Meet fallback crashes when destinationCalendar is empty

`evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` produces an empty array when no destination calendar is set, so `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is undefined. The next line dereferences `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration`, throwing a TypeError before the intended fallback to Daily can run. Previously `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration` was safely undefined. Use optional chaining, e.g. `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"`.

true_positives.golden_comment: Logic error: when externalCalendarId is provided, you're searching for a calendar where externalId === externalCalendarId, but this will always fail since you're looking for a calendar that matches itself. Should likely find by credentialId or use different logic.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Google updateEvent fallback calendar lookup always misses

When `externalCalendarId` is falsy, the fallback is `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`, which compares each calendar's externalId against null/undefined and returns undefined. `calendar.events.update` is then called with an undefined calendarId instead of the previous behavior of using `event.destinationCalendar.externalId`. The same broken pattern appears in `deleteEvent` around line 317. Legacy bookings or references without `externalCalendarId` will fail to update/delete Google Calendar events.

true_positives.golden_comment: Logic inversion in organization creation: The slug property is now conditionally set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, instead of when it's false as originally intended. This change, combined with requestedSlug still being set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, results in both properties being set when billing is enabled, and neither when disabled
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Organization creation slug condition is inverted

The diff changes `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`, and similarly changes `requestedSlug` in the metadata. This is the opposite of the previous logic and is unrelated to the destinationCalendar change. With billing disabled, new organizations no longer receive a slug, likely breaking org creation/URLs; with billing enabled, slug is now set when it was previously withheld in favor of requestedSlug. Revert this condition unless there is a separate intentional billing change.

true_positives.golden_comment: The Calendar interface now requires createEvent(event, credentialId), but some implementations (e.g., Lark/Office365) still declare createEvent(event) only—this breaks the interface contract (also applies to other locations in the PR).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Office365 createEvent always targets the first destination calendar

Even though EventManager now iterates all destination calendars and calls `createEvent` once per credential, Office365 still destructures only the first element of `event.destinationCalendar` and ignores the supplied credentialId. For a collective event with multiple hosts, every Office365 invocation targets the same first host calendar, causing duplicate events in that calendar and no event in the other hosts' Office365 calendars. The service must select the destination whose credentialId matches the current credential, similar to GoogleCalendarService. LarkCalendarService and BaseCalendarService have the same first-element-only behavior.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The optional chaining on mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration is redundant since you already check mainHostDestinationCalendar in the ternary condition.

The `credential` may be undefined when passed to `updateEvent` if `reference.credentialId` is set but the credential is not found. This can lead to a runtime error when `updateEvent` is called with an undefined credential, which should be handled to prevent crashes.

false_positives.candidate:
All Google calendar events use the first destination as organizer

`mainHostDestinationCalendar` is always the first element of `event.destinationCalendar`, and its externalId is used as the organizer email for every create/update invocation. When EventManager iterates the other host destination calendars with different credentialIds, the event is inserted into another host's calendar but the organizer attendee is still set to the first host's externalId. This can set the wrong organizer/permissions or cause Google to reject the event. The organizer email should correspond to the destination/credential being processed.

Confirmed collective bookings only schedule the first destination calendar

When a booking requiring confirmation is later confirmed, this handler rebuilds `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` from `booking.destinationCalendar` (a single Prisma relation) or the confirming user's default. The multi-host `teamDestinationCalendars` assembled at initial booking time are not persisted or reconstructed here. `handleConfirmation`/EventManager therefore creates calendar events only for the first destination, not for all hosts of a collective event.

Google Meet description patch uses undefined calendarId when no selected calendar

`calendar.events.insert` uses `selectedCalendar || "primary"`, but the subsequent `calendar.events.patch` uses `calendarId: selectedCalendar` without that fallback. When no destination in the array matches the current credentialId, `selectedCalendar` is undefined; the insert proceeds against primary, but the patch that adds the hangout link fails because the calendarId is undefined. Use the same fallback in both calls.

Paid collective bookings schedule only the first destination calendar

Both `getBooking` and `handlePaymentSuccess` build `evt.destinationCalendar` from the booking's single `destinationCalendar` or the user default. For a paid collective event, the multi-host destination calendars assembled in `handleNewBooking` are not available here and are not stored on the booking. When payment succeeds and `EventManager.create` runs, only the first/primary calendar receives the event; other hosts are not scheduled. The same issue exists in `paypal-webhook.ts`.

Recurring cancellation still deletes only one organizer calendar reference

Inside the new loop over `bookingCalendarReference`, the recurring/allRemaining branch ignores the current reference's `credentialId` and instead maps over `bookingToDelete.user.credentials` (the organizer's own credentials). For each updated booking it then calls `references.find(...)`, which returns only the first calendar reference. For a collective recurring booking with multiple host calendars, this repeats deletion of the first organizer-visible event and never deletes events belonging to the other host references. It should iterate all calendar references and use each reference's credential/externalCalendarId.

Team destination calendars are dropped when organizer has no destinationCalendar

`evt.destinationCalendar` is initialized to `null` when neither the event type nor the organizer user has a destination calendar. The team calendars are then added with `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`, which is a no-op on null. If the organizer has no destination calendar but the other collective hosts do, all collected `teamDestinationCalendars` are lost and EventManager falls back to the organizer's first connected calendar rather than creating events in the hosts' selected calendars. Initialize `evt.destinationCalendar` to an array before pushing or assign the combined array explicitly.

updateLocation creates booking references without externalCalendarId or credentialId

`referencesToCreate` now reads `result.externalId` and `result.credentialId`, but `CalendarManager.updateEvent` does not return either field (unlike `createEvent`). After editing a location, the newly created calendar `BookingReference` rows will have null `externalCalendarId` and null `credentialId`. Later cancellation/reschedule/update logic cannot identify the external calendar or credential, so it may target the wrong calendar or fail to delete/update the right event. Either `updateEvent` should return these fields, or `updateLocation` should derive them from the calendar reference being updated.

true_positives.golden_comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Missing refresh_token is replaced with string "refresh_token"

When a parsed refresh response does not include `refresh_token`, this mutates `data.refresh_token` to the literal text `"refresh_token"`. Callers like Office365 and Zoom then persist that value over the user's real refresh token, so later refreshes fail. Do not synthesize a placeholder; preserve the existing credential refresh token in the caller.

true_positives.golden_comment: The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Minimum token schema does not validate or retain expiry fields

The computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` both resolve to the same string (`[object Object]`), so the schema effectively only requires `access_token` and drops or fails to validate all other token fields. When credential sharing is enabled, any caller using this branch parses a token response into essentially `{ access_token }`, losing `expires_in`/`expiry_date`, `instance_url`, and other fields. The intended numeric expiry validation is never performed.

true_positives.golden_comment: parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Google refresh stores Zod SafeParse result instead of token data

`parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns the whole `safeParse` result (`{ success, data }`), but here `key` is that wrapper and is written to the credential directly. After a successful Google refresh, the DB key becomes `{ success: true, data: { ...tokens } }`; subsequent `googleCredentialSchema.parse(credential.key)` in the constructor fails, breaking the Google Calendar integration. Use `refreshTokenResponse.data` here.

true_positives.golden_comment: When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Sync token refresh returns an unnormalized Response

In sync mode this returns the raw `fetch` `Response`. Existing callers expect provider/axios-shaped values: Google reads `res.data.access_token`, HubSpot expects `.expiresIn`, and Zoho/Bigin expect `tokenInfo.data`. When `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` and `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are set, those code paths get `undefined` or missing properties and fail. Parse the JSON and return a consistent shape such as `{ data }`, or update every caller to consume `Response`.

true_positives.golden_comment: When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Sync token refresh returns an unnormalized Response

In sync mode this returns the raw `fetch` `Response`. Existing callers expect provider/axios-shaped values: Google reads `res.data.access_token`, HubSpot expects `.expiresIn`, and Zoho/Bigin expect `tokenInfo.data`. When `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` and `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are set, those code paths get `undefined` or missing properties and fail. Parse the JSON and return a consistent shape such as `{ data }`, or update every caller to consume `Response`.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Zoho Bigin sends credential.id as calcomUserId

`refreshOAuthTokens`'s third argument is supposed to be the Cal.com user ID, but this call passes `credentialId` (the credential row ID). When credential sharing is enabled, the parent app receives the DB credential ID as `calcomUserId` and may update the wrong user or fail to find the user. Pass `credential.userId` through to `refreshAccessToken`.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Refreshed Salesforce token is not used for the connection

The method fetches and parses a new access token, but `new jsforce.Connection(...)` is created with `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.refresh_token`, not the newly parsed token. The service instance therefore starts with the old/expired access token, causing avoidable 401s or reliance on jsforce's own auto-refresh. Use the new access token and instance URL from the refresh response.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Invalid webhook body causes unhandled ZodError

`appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)` is not wrapped in try/catch and no method check is performed. A POST with a malformed body, or a GET where `req.body` is absent, throws a `ZodError`, producing a generic 500 instead of a controlled 400. Use `safeParse` and explicitly reject non-POST methods.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

false_positives.candidate:
AES-256 key generation command yields 24 bytes, not 32

The comment says the key must be 32 bytes for AES-256 and suggests `openssl rand -base64 24`. Base64-decoding 24 input bytes yields a 24-byte key, not 32. Users following this instruction will configure an invalid/weak key. Suggest `openssl rand -base64 32` or `openssl rand -hex 32`.

Credential sync can create duplicate credentials under concurrent requests

The handler does `findFirst` and then either `update` or `create` in separate queries. Two concurrent webhook deliveries for the same user/app can both miss the existing row and insert duplicates. There is also no deterministic choice if multiple rows exist. Use a transaction plus a unique constraint/upsert keyed by `(userId, appId, type)`.

Credential sync endpoint receives no authentication

The `fetch` to `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` sends only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug` in the body. There is no secret, signature, or API key. Anyone who can reach the sync endpoint can request access tokens for arbitrary Cal.com user IDs. Since this endpoint returns third-party credentials, add an authenticated header/shared secret and enforce HTTPS.

No tests for credential sync webhook or token refresh helpers

The PR adds a security-sensitive webhook, encryption/decryption path, and shared OAuth refresh/parsing helpers used by many integrations. The checklist explicitly says no tests were added. Given the parser shape mismatches and data-loss issues, tests for success, invalid secret, malformed payload, existing/update, and sync vs local refresh would catch regressions.

Office 365 video sync refresh can overwrite stored credential with an incomplete token

When sync mode returns the documented generic payload (`access_token` plus expiry date), `responseBody.expires_in` is undefined, so `expiry_date` is set to `Date.now()` (immediately expired), and the whole `responseBody` is stored as the key. The existing `refresh_token`, `token_type`, `scope`, and `email` are not preserved, so later refreshes fail. This integration needs to merge the sync response into the existing credential instead of replacing it.

Salesforce refresh uses undefined prisma

The newly added refresh block calls `prisma.credential.update` but this file never imports `prisma` from `@calcom/prisma`. When this code runs, it will throw `ReferenceError: prisma is not defined`, and the project should also fail type-checking. Add the missing import.

Salesforce token parsing switches on global sharing flag despite fetching Salesforce directly

`parseRefreshTokenResponse(accessTokenJson, salesforceTokenSchema)` chooses the minimal schema whenever `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is set, even though this method always calls `login.salesforce.com` directly and never uses `refreshOAuthTokens`. Enabling credential sharing therefore makes Salesforce token parsing drop required fields such as `instance_url`, `id`, `issued_at`, `signature`, `scope`, and `token_type`; the stored DB key becomes incomplete and future connections can break.

Sync update does not mark credential valid again

When updating an existing credential, only `key` is changed. If that credential was previously marked `invalid: true` (for example after an invalid_grant failure), it remains invalid after syncing fresh credentials and may be skipped by integrations. The update should set `invalid: false` to reflect the new source-of-truth credential.

true_positives.golden_comment: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Blacklisted email comparison is case-sensitive

`blacklistedGuestEmails` is lowercased before comparison, but incoming `guest` values are not normalized. An email such as `Blocked@example.com` can bypass a blacklist entry of `blocked@example.com` and be added to the booking. Normalize incoming guests with `.toLowerCase()` before comparing, or better normalize in the schema/handler before all validation.

true_positives.golden_comment: The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Team admin/owner check uses AND instead of OR

`isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(...)) && (await isTeamOwner(...))`. This means a team admin who is not an owner, or an owner who is not an admin, is denied. The variable name and intended behavior indicate an OR condition; use `||` or separate the two permission checks.

true_positives.golden_comment: uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Incoming duplicate guests are not deduplicated server-side

`uniqueGuests` filters incoming guests only against existing `booking.attendees` and the blacklist; it does not deduplicate the incoming `guests` array. The server schema `z.array(z.string().email())` does not enforce uniqueness, so a caller can pass the same email twice with different casing and `createMany` will insert duplicate attendee records for the same booking, causing duplicate calendar invites and inconsistent attendee data. Deduplicate case-insensitively on the server before insertion.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
sendAddGuestsEmails ignores event-type email disable settings

Other email helpers in this file respect `eventTypeDisableHostEmail` and `eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail`, but `sendAddGuestsEmails` sends organizer and attendee emails unconditionally. Users who disabled standard host or attendee emails for an event type will still receive these add-guests notifications, violating their email preferences. Pass `eventTypeMetadata` to this function and check the relevant disable flags before sending.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.
Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.

false_positives.candidate:
Any attendee can add guests to a booking

The handler grants permission to any user whose email appears in `booking.attendees` via `isAttendee`. This exposes the tRPC mutation to every attendee, allowing them to add arbitrary emails to the booking without organizer approval. New attendees may receive calendar invitations and meeting details. Unless attendee self-service is an explicit requirement, restrict this mutation to the organizer or team admins/owners.

Calendar update uses caller credentials instead of organizer's

`getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` returns the authenticated caller's credentials, but the event belongs to `booking.user` (the organizer). The `EventManager` is then pointed at the organizer's destination calendar via `evt.destinationCalendar`. If the caller is not the organizer, this mismatch can make `updateCalendarAttendees` fail or attempt to update the wrong account's calendar. Use the booking organizer's credentials (e.g., `booking.user.credentials`) or load credentials for the organizer.

No tests cover the new addGuests mutation

This new tRPC mutation introduces authorization rules, email blacklisting, deduplication concerns, and external calendar/email side effects, but no tests are added. Missing coverage makes it easy for permission bypasses and duplicate-handling regressions to go unnoticed. Add tests for authorized and unauthorized callers, duplicate/blacklisted emails, and missing bookings.

true_positives.golden_comment: Using retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 reads a possibly stale value and can lose increments under concurrency; consider an atomic increment via Prisma (increment: 1) to avoid race conditions (also applies to the similar update in the catch block).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
retryCount updates are read-modify-write and can lose concurrent failures

Both failure updates set `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` using the value read when the reminders were loaded. If two cron invocations process the same unscheduled reminder concurrently, both can read the same retryCount and write the same value, so a failure is not recorded. Because deletion uses `retryCount > 1`, the reminder may never reach the deletion threshold and can continue being retried indefinitely. Use Prisma's atomic `retryCount: { increment: 1 }` in both updates or otherwise serialize the update.

true_positives.golden_comment: The deletion logic in scheduleSMSReminders.ts incorrectly deletes non-SMS workflow reminders (e.g., Email, WhatsApp) that have retryCount > 1. This occurs because the retryCount condition within the OR clause for deletion lacks a method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, causing it to apply to all reminder types instead of only SMS reminders, which is the intended scope of this function.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
deleteMany retryCount branch can delete non-SMS workflow reminders

The OR branch `{ retryCount: { gt: 1 } }` is not constrained by `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` or by `scheduled: false`. This handler is the SMS scheduling cron, but WorkflowReminder is shared by email and WhatsApp workflows, and retryCount is defined on the base model. Once any non-SMS reminder has retryCount > 1, this cron deletes it, causing cross-method data loss. Add `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` and likely `scheduled: false` to this branch.

false_positives.candidate:
Catch block treats every processing error as an SMS scheduling failure

The new catch block increments retryCount for any error thrown anywhere in the large try block (lines 74-187), not only for twilio.scheduleSMS. This includes template rendering, getBookerBaseUrl, prisma.profile.findFirst, and bookingMetadataSchema.parse failures. A persistent non-scheduling error will therefore increment retryCount on each run and after retryCount reaches 2 the reminder is deleted by the deleteMany query, even though the SMS was never attempted. Scope the retryCount increment to scheduleSMS failures or otherwise distinguish scheduling failures from message-preparation/DB errors.

No tests for new retry/delete behavior

The PR adds a retry count and a deletion threshold but includes no tests. Important cases are untested: scheduleSMS returning false or throwing increments retryCount, non-scheduling errors do not count as scheduling failures, retryCount > 1 deletion is scoped to SMS, and concurrent updates do not lose increments. Add unit/integration tests for this cron handler.

false_negatives.golden_comment: In getBaseConditions(), the else if (filterConditions) and final else branches are unreachable. This is because getAuthorizationConditions() always returns a non-null Prisma.Sql object, making authConditions always truthy, which means only the first two if/else if conditions are ever evaluated.

Fetching userIdsFromOrg only when teamsFromOrg.length > 0 can exclude org-level members for orgs without child teams; consider deriving from teamIds (which includes orgId) or removing the guard so org-only orgs still include member user bookings.

false_positives.candidate:
Caching tests removed without replacement

The previous `Caching` describe block tested that `getAuthorizationConditions()` and `getFilterConditions()` return the same cached result on repeated calls. Those tests were deleted in this PR, but the caching fields and `=== undefined` checks remain in the service. Caching can now regress unnoticed. Replace these tests with updated raw-SQL assertions rather than deleting them.

Removed public `findMany` method breaks existing callers

The diff deletes `InsightsBookingService.findMany` and replaces it with `getBaseConditions`. `findMany` was the method that executed the Prisma query on `bookingTimeStatusDenormalized`, allowing callers to pass `select`, additional `where` clauses, etc. Any code importing this exported service and calling `service.findMany(...)` will fail to compile after this PR. If this change is intentional, callers need to be migrated in the same PR; otherwise keep `findMany` implemented in terms of the new raw conditions or provide a compatibility adapter.

`teamId` is optional in public options even when scope is `team`

`InsightsBookingServicePublicOptions` types `teamId` as `number | undefined` for all scopes, but `insightsBookingServiceOptionsSchema` requires `teamId` for `scope: 'team'`. As a result, callers can write `{ scope: 'team', userId, orgId }` without a TypeScript error; the constructor then fails validation, sets `this.options` to `null`, and `getAuthorizationConditions()` returns `NOTHING_CONDITION`. This silently returns no data rather than surfacing the missing required option. Use a discriminated public type or throw a clear validation error.

true_positives.golden_comment: The updateManyByCredentialId call uses an empty data object, which prevents Prisma's @updatedAt decorator from updating the updatedAt timestamp. This results in inaccurate cache status tracking, as the timestamp isn't updated when the cache is refreshed. To fix this, explicitly set the updatedAt field.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Empty data passed to Prisma updateMany

The new call `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` passes an empty `data` object to `prisma.selectedCalendar.updateMany`. Prisma requires at least one field in the data argument; an empty object is rejected by validation or performs no update. This runs at the end of `fetchAvailabilityAndSetCache` after availability has already been cached, so a validation error would fail the webhook cache refresh and cause retries/error handling, while a no-op would not actually refresh `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt`. Pass `{ updatedAt: new Date() }` or remove the call if the update is not needed.

true_positives.golden_comment: logic: macOS-specific sed syntax with empty string after -i flag will fail on Linux systems
true_positives.matched_candidate:
macOS-only sed -i syntax breaks on Linux

`sed -i '' -E ...` is BSD/macOS syntax. On GNU/Linux, including WSL and many CI runners, the empty argument is treated as a backup extension or an invalid option, so updating an existing `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL` line fails. Use a portable form such as `sed -i -E` under GNU sed, `perl -pi -e`, or detect the OS before choosing the syntax.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Throwing a generic Error for authentication failures results in a 500 response in tRPC. Instead, it should return a structured TRPCError with an appropriate code, such as FORBIDDEN, to accurately reflect the error type.
Date is formatted with hardcoded 'en-US' locale instead of using the user's locale from useLocale, which can lead to incorrect date representation for users in different locales.

false_positives.candidate:
Delete cache mutation does not invalidate the connected calendars query

After `deleteCacheMutation` succeeds, it shows a toast and calls `onSuccess`, but unlike `disconnectMutation` it never calls `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.invalidate()`. The calendar list is rendered from a suspense query with `refetchOnWindowFocus: false`, so after deleting cache the old `cacheUpdatedAt` can remain visible until a manual refresh. Add invalidation to the mutation's `onSuccess` or `onSettled` so the cache status is refetched.

ENV_FILE path is relative to cwd and updates the wrong .env from repo root

`ENV_FILE="../.env"` is interpreted relative to the caller's current working directory, not the script location. The likely invocation from the repository root, `./scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh`, resolves to the parent directory of the repository, so the tunnel URL is written to the wrong `.env` or a new file is created there. Compute `SCRIPT_DIR` from `BASH_SOURCE` and derive the path from that, or use a path relative to the repository root consistently.

cacheUpdatedAt may be null/undefined when passed to Date constructor

Although this JSX is inside the `hasCache` branch, TypeScript does not narrow the separate `cacheUpdatedAt` prop from the boolean local. The prop is `Date | null | undefined`, so `new Date(cacheUpdatedAt)` is a strict null check type error and will fail type-check/build. Verify the value directly, e.g. use `cacheUpdatedAt && ...`, or format in a helper that accepts `Date | null | undefined`.

dev:cron now depends on npx fetching an undeclared tsx package

The script was changed to `npx tsx cron-tester.ts`, but `tsx` is not declared in `dependencies` or `devDependencies` for this package. `npx` can fetch the latest `tsx` from the registry at runtime, which makes the dev script non-deterministic, may fail offline, and may not work correctly under Yarn PnP. Either add `tsx` as a devDependency and invoke the local binary, or use the already-declared runner.

true_positives.golden_comment: Asynchronous functions deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder are called without await inside forEach loops. This occurs during booking rescheduling/cancellation, and workflow/workflow step deletion/updates. Consequently, scheduled workflow reminders may not be reliably cancelled, potentially leaving them active.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Workflow reminder cancellation is not awaited in cancel handler

`deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are async, but they are fired inside a `forEach` without being collected into `prismaPromises` or awaited. The previous code collected `prisma.workflowReminder.deleteMany` promises and awaited them before returning. Because this handler returns after `Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))`, the DB update that sets `cancelled = true` (or the SMS row deletion) may not complete before the serverless function is frozen after the response. A cancelled booking can therefore still have its scheduled email/SMS reminder sent.

true_positives.golden_comment: When immediateDelete is true, the deleteScheduledEmailReminder function cancels the SendGrid email but fails to delete the corresponding WorkflowReminder record from the database. This creates orphaned database entries and is inconsistent with the immediateDelete: false path, which marks the record as cancelled. The SendGrid DELETE API call is also omitted in this path.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Reschedule path bypasses deferred cancellation and leaves stale reminder rows

`deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true)` calls SendGrid immediately with `status: 'cancel'`. This is the same pattern the PR says caused the 100 pending cancellation limit: it creates a SendGrid pending cancellation until the original send date. For rescheduled bookings, the new `cancelled`/cron mechanism should be used instead. In addition, the `immediateDelete` branch returns without deleting or marking the `WorkflowReminder` DB row, so the original booking retains rows that still appear scheduled and may be retried later. The promise is also not awaited.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The 'cancelled' field is nullable, which can lead to existing records having null values instead of a default of false. This can cause incorrect behavior in the application when checking the cancellation status of reminders.

false_positives.candidate:
